correctness.rationale: On the invariant interior the shared prefactor cancels from d log N/dx. Multiplying the proposed log-derivative of Φ by x(1−x)d(x) gives a quadratic with endpoint values P and R and quadratic coefficient b−a, exactly those of W; this check also covers a=b. Positive g and W give exponential convergence N→K. The increasing Φ has endpoint limits 0 and infinity, so the invariant gives a unique interior x∞, with x−x∞ exponentially small by local inversion. The resource log-odds derivative ε(1+θ)(x−x_c) integrates to the appropriate infinite limit unless x∞=x_c, when its integral is positive and finite. If x_0≤x_c, the terminal x is strictly below x_c even at initial equality. For K>K_c and x_0>x_c, strict monotonicity yields exactly one crossing and the invariant fixes its population coordinate at K_c, not its physical time or resource height. For the calibration, Φ(3/4)=36, Φ(1/2)=2, and cancelling 2x−1 leaves x/[(1−x)(1+(1−x)^2)]. With y=1−x the primitive is log y−(1/2)log(1+y²)−arctan y, yielding the stated J. Solving n/(1−n)²=2 exp(J) and evaluating gives 0.563817739263549, consistent with the stated interior limit. The supplied script and documented checks were read, not run.

value.rationale: This gives a complete finite-capacity phase classification in a natural subclass that fixes the payoff order and isolates the role of population growth. It explains why a strictly declining cooperative fraction can still sustain the resource, gives a feedback-independent turning population and resolves the nonhyperbolic critical resource fate rather than just reproducing the known rescue phenomenon.
